newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES EASE 0.53 PCT, TESTING SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES EASE 0.53 PCT, TESTING SUPPORT.

text.p: Istanbul shares slipped lower in range-bound trade on Wednesday as the market tested support of the index at 81,000 in the absence of market moving expectations, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 fell 430.56 points, or 0.53 percent from Tuesday to close at 81,464.08 after moving between 80,984 and 82,964. Trade volume leapt to 19.27 trillion lira from 16.73 trillion lira on Tuesday.
Brokers said sellers emerged in the second session after the index was barely changed at midday.

"Sales that began in (largely state-owned petroleum refiner) Tupras in early afternoon spilled over to other issues. But the 81,000 support held. The index may continue drifting sideways with share-based activity," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
But some other brokers said the index could pierce the 81,000 level on Thursday or Friday to test major support awaited at the 80,000 mark.
The market went into range-trading after failing to break the stiff 85,000 barrier last Thursday.
The index has surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to an all-time high close of 83,772.33 on October 23, the tenth record in an uptrend which began with the breaching of the 65,000 level.
Of the 229 shares traded, 93 fell, 91 gained and 45 closed unchanged. The 85-share industrial index eased 0.25 percent to 86,354.37 and the 15-share financial index lost 1.14 percent to 78,269.86.

Actives were led by utilities Aktas Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 100,000, Cukurova Elektrik, steady at 81,000 lira and largely state-owned petroleum distributor Tupras, up 500 lira at 19,000. Together, they made up 32 percent of the total market volume.
